stem:
Which of the following processes play a part in the formation of a rainbow?
(i) Refraction
(ii) Total internal reflection
(iii) Dispersion
(iv) Interference
solution: Rainbow is formed due to the dispersion of light suffering refraction and total internal reflection (TIR) in the droplets present in the atmosphere.

stem: The terminal velocity of a small sphere of radius $a$ in a viscous liquid is proportional to
solution:
Terminal velocity in a viscous medium is given by:

$$V_T = \dfrac{2a^2(\rho - \sigma)g}{9\eta}$$

$\therefore V_T \propto a^2$

stem: A force acts on a $2$ kg object so that its position is given as a function of time as $x = 3t^2 + 5$. What is the work done by this force in first $5$ seconds?
solution:
Position, $x = 3t^2 + 5$

$\therefore$ Velocity, $v = \dfrac{dx}{dt} = 6t$

At $t = 0$, $v = 0$; at $t = 5$ s, $v = 30$ m/s

By the work-energy theorem, $W = \Delta KE = \dfrac{1}{2}mv^2 - 0 = \dfrac{1}{2}(2)(30)^2 = 900$ J

stem: A transverse wave is represented by $y = \dfrac{10}{\pi}\sin\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{T}t - \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda}x\right)$. For what value of the wavelength the wave velocity is twice the maximum particle velocity?
solution:
Amplitude $a = \dfrac{10}{\pi}$ cm

Wave velocity $= 2\times$ maximum particle velocity

i.e., $\dfrac{\omega\lambda}{2\pi} = 2a\omega = 2\cdot\dfrac{10\omega}{\pi}$

or, $\lambda = 4\pi a = 4 \times 10 = 40$ cm

stem: The reading of the ammeter for a silicon diode in the given circuit is
solution:
Silicon diode is in forward bias. Hence across the diode there is a potential barrier $\Delta V = 0.7$ V.

$$I = \dfrac{V - \Delta V}{R} = \dfrac{3 - 0.7}{200} = \dfrac{2.3}{200} = 11.5\ \text{mA}$$

stem: Energy required to move a body of mass $m$ from an orbit of radius $2R$ to $3R$ is
solution:
Change in potential energy in displacing a body from $r_1$ to $r_2$:

$$\Delta U = GMm\left[\dfrac{1}{r_1} - \dfrac{1}{r_2}\right] = GMm\left(\dfrac{1}{2R} - \dfrac{1}{3R}\right) = \dfrac{GMm}{6R}$$
notes: Printed solution uses change in PE only (not total orbital energy); key follows it.

stem: In the circuit shown, charge on the $5\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor is:
solution:
Let potential of point O be $V_0 = 0$ and of junction be $x$.

Using junction analysis, $q_1 + q_2 + q_3 = 0$:

$$2(x-6) + 4(x-6) + 5x = 0 \Rightarrow x = \dfrac{36}{11}$$

$q_3 = \dfrac{36(5)}{11} = \dfrac{180}{11} = 16.36\ \mu\text{C}$

stem: The stopping potential in the context of photoelectric effect depends on the following property of incident electromagnetic radiation
solution: The stopping potential $(V_S)$ depends upon the frequency of the incident electromagnetic radiation.
